title.th: การเปลี่ยนแปลงทางการเกษตรและปัญหาสิ่งแวดล้อม

summary.en: Investigating drivers of change, dimensions of change and local adaptation mechanisms.
summary.th: ศึกษาปัจจัยที่ขับเคลื่อนการเปลี่ยนแปลงทางการเกษตรและการปรับตัวของชุมชน ผ่านการทบทวนเอกสาร การสัมภาษณ์ และข้อมูลสถิติ ครอบคลุมปัญหาน้ำ ฝุ่นควัน ภูมิอากาศ สิทธิในที่ดิน หนี้สิน และเทคโนโลยีใหม่

paragraphs: Investigating drivers of change, dimensions of change and local adaptation mechanisms.
Methods: Literature review, interviews of key informants, statistical data.
Changing landscapes - modernization of agriculture but persistence of environmental issues:
Water scarcity (droughts) and abundance (floods)
Forest and agricultural residues burning (haze and PM 2.5)
Adaptation to climate change and mitigation
Changing livelihoods - aging farmers, decreasing population and newcomers in search of Nan specific identity (nature and culture)
Tensions about tenure rights and forest policies
Indebtedness and constraints to investments in sustainable agriculture
New technologies (drones, mechanization, etc.)

title.en: Toxic landscapes and livelihoods from chemical use in agriculture
title.th: ภูมิทัศน์และวิถีชีวิตที่ได้รับผลกระทบจากสารเคมี

summary.en: Getting out of chemical use in agriculture to reduce contaminations of the ecosystems and impacts on human health. OneHealth approaches applied to rodents in Nan. Individual interview and focus group discussions. Participatory workshops, role play games, community engagement, exploration of scenarios toward reducing pesticide use.
summary.th: ศึกษาผลกระทบจากสารเคมีทางการเกษตรต่อระบบนิเวศและสุขภาพ ผ่านการสัมภาษณ์ กลุ่มสนทนา และเกมบทบาทสมมติ เพื่อสำรวจทางเลือกในการลดการใช้สารเคมีร่วมกับชุมชน

paragraphs: Getting out of chemical use in agriculture to reduce contaminations of the ecosystems and impacts on human health. OneHealth approaches applied to rodents in Nan. Individual interview and focus group discussions. Participatory workshops, role play games, community engagement, exploration of scenarios toward reducing pesticide use.
Participatory exploration of scenarios out of chemical use: changes in techniques - practices, principles - regulations, policies changes.
Many projects promote alternative practices or behaviors, but their impact remains limited.
Impact pathway requires identifying the real drivers of change: role of knowledge, money, power in addressing wicked problems
Reflections on community engagement and its limits in a context of ageing farming population – questioning intergenerational knowledge transmission patterns

title.en: Biodiversity dynamics between forest and agriculture
title.th: พลวัตความหลากหลายทางชีวภาพระหว่างป่าและเกษตรกรรม

summary.en: Biodiversity is an important element of resilience in the socioecological systems. We propose a holistic approach across multiple scales, sectors and stakeholders to address entangled issues. How the research community engages in wicked problems through concepts such as adaptive spaces, learning centers, living labs, knowledge-scapes. How to maintain a balance between forest and agriculture in complex landscape mosaics.
summary.th: ศึกษาความสัมพันธ์ระหว่างป่า เกษตรกรรม และความหลากหลายทางชีวภาพ ตั้งแต่ป่าชุมชนและวนเกษตรจนถึงเกษตรเชิงเดี่ยว โดยพิจารณาทั้งกฎระเบียบ การจัดการทรัพยากร และวิถีชีวิต

paragraphs: Biodiversity is an important element of resilience in the socioecological systems. We propose a holistic approach across multiple scales, sectors and stakeholders to address entangled issues. How the research community engages in wicked problems through concepts such as adaptive spaces, learning centers, living labs, knowledge-scapes. How to maintain a balance between forest and agriculture in complex landscape mosaics.

Along a gradient of agricultural intensification, we analyze the impacts on biodiversity of agroforestry and community forests, regulatory frameworks, and resource management. From conflicts over resources to reorganization of upland landscapes and livelihoods, we document the changing relations between forest and agriculture through restudy of villages that were studied long ago along a gradient of agricultural intensification from community forestry to intensive monocropping.

title.en: Organic vegetable networks – Sustaining income for smallholders
title.th: เครือข่ายผักอินทรีย์และรายได้ของเกษตรกรรายย่อย

summary.en: What is the future of organic farming in Nan Province and what would be the enabling conditions of such a future? How does organic farming link with ecotourism potential of the upland province. We address these questions by investigating the past and the present of organic farming and then by mobilizing this knowledge to explore possible futures with key stakeholders.
summary.th: สำรวจเส้นทางสู่เกษตรอินทรีย์ของบุคคลและเครือข่ายในน่าน รวมถึงคุณค่าที่ผลักดันการเปลี่ยนแปลง การรับรองสินค้า การตลาด และความเชื่อมโยงกับการท่องเที่ยวเชิงนิเวศ

paragraphs: What is the future of organic farming in Nan Province and what would be the enabling conditions of such a future? How does organic farming link with ecotourism potential of the upland province. We address these questions by investigating the past and the present of organic farming and then by mobilizing this knowledge to explore possible futures with key stakeholders.

Going organic is not only a question of agronomic practices or economic development. In this research, we investigated the multiple dimensions of organic agriculture, including the underlying values of engagement in alternative practices and the challenges related to the marketing of clean products (certification, etc.). Going organic is also a lifestyle beyond agricultural practices. We study the pathways that brought individuals or collectives to different models of organic farming and explore the diversity of organic farms in Nan province.

title.en: Native Red Cows - Preserving natural and cultural heritage
title.th: วัวแดงพื้นเมืองน่านกับมรดกทางธรรมชาติและวัฒนธรรม

summary.en: The Nan Red Cow landrace is a domesticated, locally adapted, native species of cattle that has developed over time, through adaptation to its natural and cultural environment, and due to isolation from other populations of the species. A research-action program started 10 years ago to characterize the genetic strain of the Nan red cow and then to preserve this traditional landrace as an agricultural heritage of Nan Province. Following training sessions, pure breed cows were given to members of a farmers’ network who shared the calves born to other members of the network to gradually improve the genetics of the native cow population.
summary.th: ศึกษาการอนุรักษ์วัวแดงพื้นเมืองน่านผ่านเครือข่ายเกษตรกร การฝึกอบรม และการแบ่งปันลูกวัว พร้อมประเมินบทบาทขององค์ความรู้ทางวิทยาศาสตร์และการมีส่วนร่วมระยะยาวของชุมชน

paragraphs: The Nan Red Cow landrace is a domesticated, locally adapted, native species of cattle that has developed over time, through adaptation to its natural and cultural environment, and due to isolation from other populations of the species. A research-action program started 10 years ago to characterize the genetic strain of the Nan red cow and then to preserve this traditional landrace as an agricultural heritage of Nan Province. Following training sessions, pure breed cows were given to members of a farmers’ network who shared the calves born to other members of the network to gradually improve the genetics of the native cow population.

Our outcome evidencing study investigates the transformative role of the scientific knowledge mobilized by Chulalongkorn University’s Center for Social Engagement in this intervention. It also explores the benefits and constraints related to the different intervention mechanisms to see to what extent they can support the long-term community engagement. The study feeds contemporary scientific debates about transformative research and the role of scientific knowledge in supporting local development.

title.en: La Oon Nan – Sensitizing the youth to biodiversity values
title.th: ละอ่อนน่านกับการเรียนรู้คุณค่าความหลากหลายทางชีวภาพ

summary.en: Scientific research conducted on community forests in Nan Province have revealed the value of the ecosystem services they provide. However, this rich body of knowledge still needed to be passed on to the younger generation – to drive their engagement in forest conservation. The research entitled “La Oon Nan or Nan Talents” was implemented by the Faculty of Science of Chulalongkorn University. It created shared learning among youths about community forest management.
summary.th: ส่งต่อความรู้เรื่องป่าชุมชนสู่เยาวชนผ่านเกมจำลองสถานการณ์ การสำรวจคาร์บอนและความหลากหลายทางชีวภาพ และการสื่อสารผลการเรียนรู้ร่วมกับชุมชนและหน่วยงานท้องถิ่น

paragraphs: Scientific research conducted on community forests in Nan Province have revealed the value of the ecosystem services they provide. However, this rich body of knowledge still needed to be passed on to the younger generation – to drive their engagement in forest conservation. The research entitled “La Oon Nan or Nan Talents” was implemented by the Faculty of Science of Chulalongkorn University. It created shared learning among youths about community forest management.

The participatory action-research comprised three main stages: (i) sensitization of school children and local youths on forest multiple values through gaming simulation approaches, (ii) involved community members in monitoring forest resources through direct measurements of carbon and biodiversity, and (iii) shared the results with community members and local authorities through creative communication approaches. The evaluation study of “La Oon Nan” assessed the impact pathway of the transformative pedagogy that was applied by the action-research described here above over a ten-year period in Nan Province.

title.en: Learning centers as islands of agroecological coherence
title.th: ศูนย์เรียนรู้กับการเชื่อมโยงแนวปฏิบัติทางนิเวศเกษตร

summary.en: Sustainable agriculture has long been supported by multiple actor networks that operate over a large range of intervention mechanisms. In the context of Nan Province, different sectors, such as private enterprises, government agencies, royal projects, scientific researchers, Buddhist temples, individual farmers or local communities are involved in agricultural extension projects that support alternative agroecological practices. Some initiatives are time bound; others are deeply rooted in specific locations and durably engaged with local communities.
summary.th: ศึกษาศูนย์เรียนรู้ในจังหวัดน่านในฐานะพื้นที่เรียนรู้จากการปฏิบัติจริง โดยสำรวจประวัติ เครือข่าย แนวปฏิบัติ และรูปแบบการดำเนินงานที่สนับสนุนการเปลี่ยนผ่านทางนิเวศเกษตร

paragraphs: Sustainable agriculture has long been supported by multiple actor networks that operate over a large range of intervention mechanisms. In the context of Nan Province, different sectors, such as private enterprises, government agencies, royal projects, scientific researchers, Buddhist temples, individual farmers or local communities are involved in agricultural extension projects that support alternative agroecological practices. Some initiatives are time bound; others are deeply rooted in specific locations and durably engaged with local communities.

We consider these learning centers as living laboratories that offer concrete support to experiential learning beyond the traditional activities of agricultural extension services. Our survey of learning centers distributed across the Nan province leads to a description of their historical pathways, social networks, practices, and business models. We study the underlying social networks and higher-level coalitions that may synergize their actions toward an agroecology movement.

title.en: From community engagement to agroecology movement
title.th: จากการมีส่วนร่วมของชุมชนสู่ขบวนการนิเวศเกษตร

summary.en: Agroecology definitions traditionally distinguish three interrelated dimensions: science, practice and movement. This research addresses the third dimension of social engagement toward an agroecological transition. That means going beyond demonstrations and prototyping of alternative agricultural practices to broad-based transformations engaging the whole society.
summary.th: ศึกษาการเชื่อมโยงวิทยาศาสตร์ แนวปฏิบัติ และขบวนการทางสังคม โดยเรียนรู้จากความร่วมมือของชุมชน ภาครัฐ ธุรกิจ และนักวิชาการในจังหวัดน่าน

paragraphs: Agroecology definitions traditionally distinguish three interrelated dimensions: science, practice and movement. This research addresses the third dimension of social engagement toward an agroecological transition. That means going beyond demonstrations and prototyping of alternative agricultural practices to broad-based transformations engaging the whole society.

Nan province has a long history of civil society movement that built an extraordinary culture of community service and trust under resource scarcity. Several scholars have analysed the factors that supported the province-wide movements, including the roles played by local leaders. They emphasized cross-sector collaboration between community, government, business, NGOs, and academics for sustainable development. Many lessons learnt may support current policy dialogues and community engagements towards the emergence of an agroecology movement.

title.th: การเรียนรู้ผ่านประสบการณ์เพื่อพัฒนานิเวศเกษตร

summary.en: In the context of Nan Province, we have shown the key roles of: (i) strong leadership driven by higher values and principles, (ii) adaptive spaces favoring synergies across multiple sectors, and (iii) governance models supportive to knowledge co-creation. They are crucial elements of an agroecological transition capable of dealing with the long list of “wicked problems” that have persisted in time. Today, a large part of the farmers is still dependent on intensive monocropping for their survival and many of them are trapped in the vicious circle of indebtedness. While this agricultural population is ageing and intensive monocropping is still covering large areas of the province, new hopes come in the form of “newcomers” who develop alternative practices better aligned with the principles of agroecology. To support intergenerational solidarity and experiential education, we co-designed two agroecological curriculum dedicated to three types of learners: high school students, community members and university students.
summary.th: พัฒนาการเรียนรู้ร่วมกันระหว่างนักเรียน ชุมชน และนักศึกษา ผ่านหลักสูตรที่ออกแบบร่วมกัน เพื่อสนับสนุนการสร้างความรู้ การเรียนรู้ระหว่างรุ่น และการเปลี่ยนผ่านทางนิเวศเกษตร

paragraphs: In the context of Nan Province, we have shown the key roles of: (i) strong leadership driven by higher values and principles, (ii) adaptive spaces favoring synergies across multiple sectors, and (iii) governance models supportive to knowledge co-creation. They are crucial elements of an agroecological transition capable of dealing with the long list of “wicked problems” that have persisted in time. Today, a large part of the farmers is still dependent on intensive monocropping for their survival and many of them are trapped in the vicious circle of indebtedness. While this agricultural population is ageing and intensive monocropping is still covering large areas of the province, new hopes come in the form of “newcomers” who develop alternative practices better aligned with the principles of agroecology. To support intergenerational solidarity and experiential education, we co-designed two agroecological curriculum dedicated to three types of learners: high school students, community members and university students.
